blocks.orig: Whether you are planning to climb Mount Kilimanjaro, explore the northern national parks or live your best life on Zanzibar, this safari extension is perfect to make your trip to Tanzania complete.
blocks.html: Are you planning to climb Mount Kilimanjaro, visit the northern national parks or enjoy yourself on Zanzibar? Whichever it is, this safari extension rounds off your Tanzania trip perfectly.

blocks.orig: Nyerere National Park, previously called Selous Game Reserve, is certainly one of the highlights among Tanzania’s southern national parks. A highly recommended activity during your trip is the boat safari on the Rufiji River. The river runs through the entire park, and it is easy to spot thirsty wildlife that gathers along its shores.
blocks.html: Nyerere National Park, formerly known as Selous Game Reserve, is without doubt one of the highlights of Tanzania’s southern national parks. One activity we highly recommend on your trip is a boat safari on the Rufiji River. The river flows through the whole park, so it is easy to see thirsty wildlife gathering on its banks.

blocks.orig: This private safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace, exactly the way you like it. You will have a private safari vehicle and guide.
blocks.html: On this private safari you are free to travel at your own pace, just the way you like. You get your own safari vehicle and guide.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: Lots of travellers want to know which time of year is best for Tanzania. Honestly, no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to go, and your interests and budget. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our Tanzania safaris you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality: the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you decide. Perhaps you would like to catch the animals at their busiest around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or you’d rather round off the day at the pool; it’s your call. Because Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments throughout the day, you will have lots of chances to watch animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, definitely. Tanzania is known as one of the top destinations for meeting the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo can all be seen here in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country to travel in. The atmosphere is hospitable, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are welcoming, and as anywhere else in the world it is sensible to take ordinary precautions, like keeping an eye on your belongings. Thanks to Tanzania’s natural beauty and its warm, welcoming people, it is a wonderful place to visit.

blocks.orig: Welcome to Tanzania! Upon your arrival at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly and knowledgeable guide will be eagerly waiting to warmly welcome you. He will be readily available to assist you and ensure a smooth transfer to your hotel. Sit back, relax, and let us take care of all your travel needs, providing you with a memorable and unforgettable experience in Tanzania.
blocks.html: Welcome to Tanzania! When you arrive at Dar es Salaam Airport, our friendly and knowledgeable guide is looking forward to greeting you warmly. He is there to help you with anything you need and makes sure your transfer to your hotel goes smoothly. Lean back and relax while we look after all your travel arrangements, so your time in Tanzania becomes a memorable experience.

blocks.orig: Today you discover the jungle, savannah and river sides of the vast Nyerere National Park (previously the Selous Game Reserve) - an amazing place for game drives. This park in southern Tanzania has fewer visitors than the northern parks but boasts elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and more. It's the second largest park in the country after Serengeti National Park, so be prepared to cover some miles!
blocks.html: Today you set out on game drives through the jungle, the savannah and along the rivers of vast Nyerere National Park (once known as the Selous Game Reserve), a superb area for spotting wildlife. Fewer people visit this southern Tanzanian park than the parks in the north, yet it is home to elephants, hippos, crocodiles, lions, leopards, giraffes, the endangered rhino, the rare African wild dog and more. In size it is second only to Serengeti National Park, so be ready to travel quite a distance!

blocks.orig: During a boat safari of 2 - 3 hours, you discover the scenic Rufiji River and its animals. From the boat, you might spot hippos, crocodiles, monkeys, many birds AND a beautiful sunset! For this sunset, you set foot on one of the small sandbanks on the river, where you can stretch your legs or enjoy a drink while the sun sets in this magical environment. There is nothing more beautiful than the serenity of a river completely surrounded by nature at this golden hour of the day.
blocks.html: On a boat safari lasting 2 - 3 hours, you explore the scenic Rufiji River and its wildlife. From the boat you may see hippos, crocodiles, monkeys, lots of birds AND a beautiful sunset! To watch the sunset, you step onto one of the river's small sandbanks, where you can stretch your legs or have a drink as the sun goes down in this magical setting. Nothing is more beautiful than the calm of a river surrounded entirely by nature at this golden hour.

blocks.orig: The last day! Enjoy the final moments of your holiday before heading to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam for your flight home. Having second thoughts? Extending your holiday to paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia is also possible!
blocks.html: This is your last day! Savour the closing moments of your trip, then make your way to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam to catch your flight home. Having doubts about leaving? It is also possible to add time on paradise islands like Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia to your holiday!
